MAJOR: `Registry.GetForTenant` only rejects an empty tenant string, then calls the unscoped `Get(name)`; it cannot detect a cross-tenant lookup (control C-6/AC-4 still unmet) and `TestRegistryTenantScoped` only asserts empty-vs-nonempty tenant, proving no tenant binding.

`DefaultRegistry` gates webhook registration on `ResolveHMACKey("")` (the env default only), so subscriptions that carry a per-subscription `auth_ref` key — explicitly the primary key with the env value as *default* — get no webhook transport at all; AC-1/AC-2 cannot be met for auth_ref-only configs.

Delta changes `sendEmail` to accept `sub` but the body still sends `To: n.SMTP.From` (self); the signature-only change leaves the subscriber never receiving email, so AC-1's "subscriber receives events through … notify/email transports" remains unmet in the very hunk that attempted the fix.

`secrets.go` (providing `ResolveHMACKey`) is still absent from the full candidate's changed files while this delta adds a new call site in `registry.go`; the package remains non-compilable, so all new delta tests/AC evidence are unverifiable (prior BLOCKER, still PENDING).
MINOR: 429 `Retry-After` parsing accepts only integer delta-seconds; the RFC 7231 HTTP-date form is ignored, so the failure-matrix `retry max(backoff, retry-after)` contract is only partially honored.
`wait` from `Retry-After` is applied unbounded with no cap and no metric/log when it overrides the backoff (violates "bounded" retry pacing and observability expectations).

Dispatcher uses a duck-typed `interface{ RetryAfter() time.Duration }` assertion instead of a shared exported error contract in `edpdata`; any future wrapping of the transport error silently drops the retry-after signal.

`DefaultRegistry` silently omits the webhook transport with no startup validation log/metric, so operators cannot diagnose why webhook delivery stopped (guardrail: startup config-shape validation + observability).
NIT: `sub` parameter of `sendEmail` is unused (only the signature changed), which will trip unused-parameter lint and contradicts `no-dead-code` evidence.

A 429 without `Retry-After` now returns `retryAfterError{wait:0}` with message "webhook status 429" instead of "webhook transient status 429", diverging log/DLQ classification strings for the same condition.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly implements `retry max(backoff, retry-after)` plumbing and a first-pass tenant-check helper, but the new registry API is cosmetic (no real tenant scoping), webhook registration is gated on the wrong key source, and the notify recipient fix was left signature-only — the approved contract is still not met.
Top risks: unresolved compile gap (`secrets.go`), per-subscription auth_ref key ignored at registry construction, and email that never reaches a subscriber.
